newsitem.title: USA: General Mills Q2 cereal share hits 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: General Mills Q2 cereal share hits 25 pct.

text.p: General Mills Inc said Thursday that its domestic market share for Big G cereals, measured in pounds of cereal sold, hit 25 percent in the fiscal second quarter.
A year ago, its share of U.S. grocery cereal sales was 23.5 percent.

General Mills said three new products -- Betty Crocker Cinnamon Streusel and Dutch Apple cereals and French Toast Crunch -- posted good initial performance in the second quarter, supported by strong introductory marketing.
These new cereals, along with Frosted Cheerios introduced in September 1995, accounted for nearly 2.5 points of the market share.
General Mills said its Big G cereals recorded volume gains of more than 10 percent in the second quarter and seven percent through the first six-months of fiscal 1997.

The company said strong second quarter volume for established cereals was up seven percent. It credited the strong performance of brands featured in its annual "Salute to Savings" merchandising event and the success of a sample-size merchandising program.

General Mills said ready-to-eat cereal category volume, measuring all outlets including grocery stores and mass merchandisers, grew nearly one percent during the second quarter and 1.5 percent in the first half.
The company said strong unit volume drove its market share for the first half of the year up 1.5 points to 24.3 percent.
